newsitem.title: UK: UK's Camelot to explore not-for-profit lottery.
newsitem.headline: UK's Camelot to explore not-for-profit lottery.

text.p: Sir George Russell, chairman of UK national lottery operator Camelot, said on Monday he had agreed with the government to explore ways of turning the lottery into a not-for-profit organisation.

Russell told reporters he would submit ideas to National Heritage Secretary Chris Smith within six weeks with a possible view to establishing not-for-profit status before Camelot's licence to run the lottery expires in 2001.
Smith had summoned Russell to express the government's outrage that Camelot's executive salary bill rose 40 percent in the year to March while the sums it raised for good causes fell.
Smith repeated last week the new Labour government's determination to hand over the lottery to a non-profit making organisation when Camelot's licence expires.

"We understand that there is obviously going to be a change in the shape of the lottery for the future and we've offered to work with the government to provide for them within six weeks our views on the shape of a lottery that is without profit in the long-term and possibly changing in the shorter," Russell said.

He said he was powerless to change directors' contracts, which had been freely entered into, but said Camelot would pay out of its profits into a charity fund a sum equal to the bonuses received by the firm's directors in the past year.
